data.title: Protesters counter Trump’s Kennedy Center demolition threat
data.description: WASHINGTON - Protesters formed a human chain on Friday around the Kennedy Center, the Washington arts hub that US President Donald Trump threatened to demolish unless his name is restored to it.

data.title: A family affair
data.description: Mah Damba is one of Mali's most revered traditional griot singers, although she is not as well known outside the country as her famous aunt Fanta Damba.

data.title: Chasing the groove
data.description: After post-rock emerged as a major indie sub-genre, exploding in popularity from the early 2000s onwards and inspiring countless bands in Thailand to follow its path, few could have imagined that Tortoise, one of the genre's most revered names, would finally make it to Bangkok.

data.title: Anti-Assad music star makes triumphant return to Syria
data.description: DAMASCUS - Syrian singer Assala Nasri has made a triumphant return to Damascus with a sold-out concert following 15 years of exile due to her opposition to ousted ruler Bashar al-Assad.

data.title: Miss Universe Thailand, Indonesia, Vietnam, Laos, Malaysia, Singapore franchises disputed
data.description: The Miss Universe organisation is facing a major dispute over national franchise agreements, after a document issued in its name stated that JKN Universe LLC does not recognise several national franchise arrangements, including the Miss Universe Thailand franchise for 2025–2029.

data.title: Doom Loop? Ed Sheeran struggles against Gaza tide
data.description: PARIS - Facing boycott calls and desertions, British singer Ed Sheeran has been left with a career crisis that underlines how even the world's biggest stars are being sucked into the politics of the war in Gaza.

data.title: Message received and understood
data.description: Apple TV has just dropped a new buddy action comedy, Mayday, starring Ryan Reynolds and Kenneth Branagh, who have teamed up with Game Night (2018) directing duo John Francis Daley and Jonathan Goldstein.

data.title: Two unseen Monet paintings to be auctioned in Paris
data.description: PARIS - Two paintings by the Impressionist master Claude Monet that have never been shown in public are to be sold in Paris next month by the billionaire Schlumberger family of France, auction house Sotheby’s said Thursday.

data.title: Som tam and beer: Lisa lights up American TV
data.description: Thai-born global pop star Lalisa “Lisa” Manobal introduced US talk-show host Jimmy Fallon to som tam and her “special” cocktail made with Korean soju, Thai Chang beer and Sprite as she promoted her forthcoming mini-album on his popular late-night show.

data.title: ‘Oasis: Don't Look Back in Anger’ definitely lives up to title
data.description: For most of the 15 years since their split in 2009, the narrative surrounding the legendary British rock band Oasis has been “they are great, but …”. Now, with their Oasis Live ’25 Tour and its subsequent documentary “Oasis: Don’t Look Back in Anger”, Noel and Liam Gallagher are back together to add another “great” after the “but” and reshape the band’s narrative.

data.title: Exquisite woodwork  on show at 'Cellulose II'
data.description: Eight Thai and international artists are showing their timber talents at "Cellulose II: Wood – Wood You? Exploring The Life Of A Living Material" at Atta Gallery, until Oct 25.

data.title: 'PULSE 2' gathers seven  artists in Singapore
data.description: Visitors to Singapore are invited to catch up with new works by seven artists from the Lion City and Indonesia at Haridas Contemporary gallery until Oct 11.

data.title: More activists call out Ed Sheeran over Palestine
data.description: STOCKHOLM - Swedish activist Greta Thunberg and other activists have called out British superstar Ed Sheeran after the rapper Macklemore was dropped from his tour for making pro-Palestinian comments while performing.

data.title: The ultimate pencil case for serious artists
data.description: Rimowa is putting a luxury spin on the artist’s toolkit with its latest collaboration with German stationery house Faber-Castell, transforming its signature aluminium luggage design into a limited-edition case for drawing supplies.

data.title: The architecture of belief
data.description: For nine years, filmmaker Sompot Chidgasornpongse carried the story of 9 Temples To Heaven with him. The basic idea remained unchanged -- a large family travels to nine temples in a single day to make merit for their grandmother, who has been warned that she may die before her birthday. But almost everything around that premise continued to evolve.

data.title: Artists exit Sheeran tour in solidarity with Macklemore pro-Palestinian comments
data.description: LOS ANGELES (UNITED STATES) - The artist Finneas and three other supporting acts announced they had quit British superstar Ed Sheeran's tour on Tuesday, after rapper Macklemore was dropped for making pro-Palestinian comments while performing.

data.title: Nat Yontararak debuts his Rabbit's Tale piano suite
data.description: OLive Music presents the world premiere of Rabbit's Tale piano suite, a neurodiverse-friendly performance by Nat Yontararak, at Sala Sudasiri Sobha, Lat Phrao 41 yaek 7-2, on Sunday at 4pm.

data.title: Nintendo marks 40 years of Zelda with  Ocarina Of Time remake for Switch 2
data.description: In celebration of The Legend Of Zelda's 40th anniversary, a remake of the Ocarina Of Time instalment is launching on Nov 5 for the Nintendo Switch 2.

data.title: Moulin Rouge! The Musical brings a  Belle Epoque love story to Bangkok
data.description: For an evening of dazzling spectacle, romance and iconic music, Thai theatre audiences can soon step into the glittering world of Paris with Moulin Rouge! The Musical, the stage adaptation of Baz Luhrmann's acclaimed 2001 film.

data.title: 'Widow's Bay' and 'The Pitt' tipped for success at Emmy Awards
data.description: LOS ANGELES (UNITED STATES) - The brightest stars in television are set to walk the red carpet Monday at the Emmy Awards, with horror-comedy series "Widow's Bay" and gritty hospital drama "The Pitt" expected to win big.

data.title: Artist Kitti Narod returns  with first solo show in 5 years
data.description: Thai artist Kitti Narod returns to Bangkok for his first solo exhibition in five years, "A Place We Share", at Tang Contemporary Art, until Oct 18.

data.title: Ecocide in focus at 'Negotiating Danger'
data.description: The commodification of natural and human resources is portrayed in "Negotiating Danger: Contemporary Javanese Scrolls", which is running at the Curved Wall, 4th floor of Bangkok Art and Culture Centre, Pathumwan intersection, until Sunday.

data.title: Celine Dion makes long-awaited return to stage in Paris
data.description: PARIS (FRANCE) - Celine Dion wept tears of joy on Saturday as she fulfilled her dream of returning to the stage after years battling a rare neurological disorder, with a sell-out concert in Paris.

data.title: Danish WWII drama wins top prize at Venice festival
data.description: VENICE (ITALY) - The Venice Film Festival awarded its top prize on Saturday to a Danish-made drama about a woman trying to hide a wartime relationship with a Nazi -- the only feature film with a female director in the competition.

data.title: Nene Royal rocking Phuket before AGT final
data.description: Local busker-turned-rock star Nene Royal is inviting fans to attend her live show on Saturday night at Naka Night Market, where she began her music journey in her home province of Phuket — her final show before she flies to the United States to compete in the America’s Got Talent final.

data.title: Tackling fraud
data.description: Ton instructs his grandma not to answer unknown phone calls. However, the complacent, tech-savvy teenager ends up falling prey to a scam himself. When he downloads a fake computer program, scammers blackmail him by threatening to share his nude photos.

data.title: Dior meets A24 in a two-year partnership
data.description: Dior is stepping into the world of theatre and independent cinema through a new two-year partnership with A24, bringing the renowned French fashion house into New York’s historic Cherry Lane Theatre as a principal partner.

data.title: Indian filmmaker Anuparna Roy: blocked at home, feted in Europe
data.description: VENICE — Independent Indian filmmaker Anuparna Roy, whose first film won a top prize at the Venice Film Festival last year, told Agence France-Presse ( AFP ) that it had been blocked by censors and would not be shown in her home country.

data.title: Japan feminist theatre fights misogyny in 'cute' fashion
data.description: TOKYO — Donning doll-like dresses with voluminous skirts, young women on stage roar in rage about rape and sexism they experienced in Japan, using theatre and "cute" fashion to denounce male-dominated society.

data.title: The paradox of death
data.description: Uruphong Raksasad has returned with the camera to capture the vanishing countryside in Thailand, a place where generations once shared history, values and resources, though not all equally benefited from it. In Songsakan, villagers join a funeral procession to transport a body to the cremation ground. Through this, Uruphong quietly observes his childhood memory in the midst of change.

data.title: Stray Kids' 'World Tour '  comes to Impact Arena for 2 nights
data.description: Stray Kids will bring their "World Tour " to Impact Arena for two spectacular nights. Live Nation Tero announced the global K-pop powerhouse will perform in Bangkok on Jan 16-17, with tickets available via ticketmaster.co.th from Sept 21.

data.title: Running on empty
data.description: The Runner, a new thriller film on Prime Video, has the former Wonder Woman Gal Gadot playing a mother forced into a madman's game to save her son with one simple task -- running.

data.title: Israeli-made film about Gaza gets 25-minute ovation at Venice premiere
data.description: VENICE - A chilling new documentary about Israel's AI-powered mass killing of civilians in Gaza from two Oscar-winning Israeli filmmakers received a 25-minute ovation at its premiere at the Venice Film Festival on Thursday.

data.title: A new thread in Thai heritage
